Desk rules for the long cycle
Everyone on the desk should know the plain rules
Companion Animal Travel Desk: routine care and clear handling

This section helps the desk team give calm, steady support for travelers with companion animals from booking through pickup. Staff should listen first, confirm the animal type and travel plan, and keep each case moving with care and accuracy.

Bookings must be checked against the current carrier and document rules before any space is confirmed. <<FACT F070>> If a case involves a rabbit, the team should follow the inserted guidance without adding extra promises or guesses. When the traveler brings a bird, staff must review the health papers and watch for missing or unclear details. <<FACT F083>> The inserted guidance must be used as written, and no one should try to shorten it, paraphrase it, or set aside the requirement when the trip feels simple.

The desk should explain what the traveler needs to bring, how the animal will be accepted, and what will happen at the skyport. Keep the tone warm and steady, especially when a traveler is anxious or unfamiliar with the process. If a crate, carrier, or document does not meet the rule set, say so plainly and offer the next acceptable step. Do not make exceptions on the spot, and do not accept informal assurances in place of required papers or approved equipment.

When a case changes, update the record at once so the care team, the passenger service staff, and the pickup side all have the same information. If a traveler such as Andre Vega or Elena Andersson asks for help with a companion animal, give the same careful guidance you would give any other customer, and keep private details limited to staff who need them. If the animal is named Archie, use the name with respect in conversation, but keep the file notes factual and brief.

For unclear cases, check with the senior coordinator before confirming travel. If the issue concerns handling, health, or acceptance at the skyport, contact the operations lead and pause the booking until you receive direction.
